alignments.note: Presentative dummy there belongs to the verb's unit (rule 17); up is the phrasal particle of went up, so the head stays on the verb (rule 44).
Directive he fused with its host in the single word thither, headed on the morpheme carrying the lexeme (rules 30, 32).
Subject pronoun realizes the verb's person and number (rule 17).
Preposition fused with its construct noun in one English word; head on the construct (rules 23, 30).

The construct noun takes only its own word. Corrected: the phrase's single the is not a supplied determiner on the construct, because an article morpheme stands on the rectum and takes it first (rule 29).

Corrected from unrepresented. The rectum is rendered anarthrously, so English fronts the phrase's single the to its left edge, and the article morpheme on the toponym takes it; rule 29's proper-name paragraph rules exactly this phrase shape.
Relational of belongs to the rectum (rule 19).

review_notes: Corrected: the men of Ai writes one the, and the article on the toponym takes it under rule 29 rather than being marked unrepresented beside a supplied the on the construct. Rule 29's proper-name paragraph cites the same phrase shape ('anshe beth el we-ha-'ai -> The men of Beth el and Ai), and its transliteration rider does not reach Ai, which the ASV does not spell with its article.

The remaining divisions are unchanged: thither fuses the directive he with its host (rules 30, 32), lifne fuses with its preposition headed on the construct (rules 23, 30), and there ... up stays with the verb (rules 17, 44).
